business_summary: Visa runs the world's largest electronic payments network (VisaNet). It does NOT lend money or issue cards; banks issue Visa-branded cards and Visa moves the authorization, clearing and settlement messages between the shopper's bank and the merchant's bank. It earns a small fee on each transaction (data processing revenue), a fee on the dollar volume that flows over the network (service revenue), a higher-margin fee on cross-border/international payments, and a fast-growing 'other revenue' line from value-added services - all partly offset by incentives paid to banks. In the quarter ended 2026-06-30 Visa processed 71.7 billion transactions (+10% YoY) and payments volume crossed $4 trillion for the first time. Revenue compounds with global consumer spending plus the long migration from cash and checks to digital payments, at ~61% operating margins and almost no incremental cost per transaction. No new financial filing since the Q3 FY2026 8-K; FY2026 Q4/full-year results are scheduled for 2026-10-27 after the close.

moat.type: Network effect + global scale + brand trust + high switching costs; near-duopoly with Mastercard (the two control roughly 77% of the US credit-card market)

valuation.method: Average of two methods via code/valuation.py, inputs UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-17 thesis because no new financial filing exists (Q4 FY2026 results are due 2026-10-27). (1) P/E: TTM GAAP diluted EPS $11.76 (Q4 FY25 $2.62 + Q1 FY26 $3.03 + Q2 $3.14 + Q3 $2.97) x 24/28/32 = $282/$329/$376. (2) FCF yield: TTM FCF/share $10.93 at 5.2%/4.3%/3.6% = $210/$254/$304. Combined band $246.22 / $291.73 / $339.97. Per the 2026-09-17 playbook rule, fair value was NOT raised: the only new fundamental item since the last refresh, the PBOC 'application to prepare' approval for China domestic clearing (announced 2026-10-13), carries no revenue yet, no timeline and no disclosed size, so it cannot be cited as a changed input. CROSS-CHECK on TTM non-GAAP EPS $12.78 x 24/28/32 = $307/$358/$409: even on the friendliest earnings measure, $408.51 sits right at the HIGH end. At $408.51 the stock trades at 34.7x TTM GAAP EPS, 32.0x non-GAAP EPS and a ~2.7% TTM FCF yield, ~40% ABOVE our GAAP base fair value (margin of safety -40.0%). The price rose ~10.5% since 2026-09-17 ($369.51) with no change in reported fundamentals - the gap widened purely through multiple expansion. V IS OVERVALUED ON OUR FRAMEWORK AND IS NOT A BUY TODAY. Buy zone: ~$257 (12% MoS) or ~$239 (cautious 18% MoS) on current inputs.

bull_case: Wide-moat near-duopoly: VisaNet's global web of issuers, merchants and acquirers is effectively impossible to replicate; no new entrant can match its acceptance footprint (200+ countries) or the trust of the brand.

Growth has accelerated, not slowed: net revenue rose 15% in Q1 FY2026, 17% in Q2 and 14% in Q3 (nine-month revenue +15.3% YoY), with payments volume +10%, total cross-border volume +13% and processed transactions +10% in constant dollars in Q3 FY2026.
Exceptional economics: ~60.7% TTM GAAP operating margin, ~38% ROIC, capex of only ~$1.6B on $44.5B of revenue, and ~$21.0B of TTM free cash flow.
Value-added services are scaling fast - 'other revenue' grew 45% YoY to $1.496B in Q3 FY2026 and data processing revenue grew 17% - diversifying away from pure swipe economics.

The biggest legal overhang is largely resolved: on 2026-06-09 the court approved the ~$38B US merchant interchange settlement, replacing an open-ended risk with known terms (a 10bp credit interchange cut for five years, a 1.25% standard consumer card cap for eight years, and merchant surcharging/steering rights). Interchange itself is paid to issuing banks, not to Visa.

Fortress balance sheet (net debt only ~0.35x EBITDA) and aggressive capital return: $16.430B of buybacks plus $3.852B of dividends in nine months, with $28.4B of repurchase authorisation remaining at 2026-06-30 - the share count keeps shrinking.
Visa is positioning itself inside, not against, the stablecoin and agentic-commerce shift rather than being disintermediated by it.

New since last refresh: on 2026-10-13 Visa announced the People's Bank of China approved its 'Application to Prepare' a domestic bank card clearing business (applied May 2020). This is a long-dated optionality on the world's largest card market, which UnionPay has dominated, but it is preparation only: Visa must finish preparations within a year and then apply again for a full licence. Mastercard's JV took ~4 years from a similar step to processing (2020 -> 2024).
risks: VALUATION IS THE PRIMARY RISK, AND IT HAS WORSENED. At $408.51 (Alpaca, 2026-10-20) the stock is ~40% above our GAAP base fair value of $291.73 and ~20% above the top of our band ($339.97); it is at the top even of the non-GAAP cross-check ($408.96). It trades at 34.7x TTM GAAP EPS ($11.76), 32.0x TTM non-GAAP EPS ($12.78), a ~2.7% FCF yield, and a dividend yield of ~0.66% ($0.670 quarterly). The stock rose ~10.5% since 2026-09-17 and ~13% in two weeks into a 52-week closing high, a run driven by sentiment (China headline, earnings run-up) rather than any new reported number. The 12% margin-of-safety rule needs ~$257, about 37% below today.

Event risk one week out: Q4 FY2026 results on 2026-10-27 arrive with the stock at an all-time-high multiple for our band and technically overbought after a ~13% two-week run. Any miss on operating margin, client incentives or FY2027 guidance could reprice the stock sharply. Equally, a strong report would raise TTM EPS/FCF and lift our band legitimately - so the right move is to wait for the filing, not to anticipate it.

China optionality may be over-priced: the PBOC step is preparatory only, no operating date has been given, UnionPay is entrenched domestically, and the approval was widely reported as politically timed ahead of a Xi-Trump meeting at APEC in Shenzhen - so it can be slowed by geopolitics as easily as it was granted.

Rising rates work directly against this stock. The Fed has just hiked to 3.75-4.00% with inflation at 3.4%; a higher risk-free rate compresses the multiple investors will pay for a long-duration compounder, and Visa's own interest expense jumped to $194M in Q3 FY2026 from $39M a year earlier.

Cost growth is outrunning revenue growth. Q3 FY2026 GAAP operating expenses rose 19% (non-GAAP +17%) against 14% revenue growth; personnel expense rose 40% to $2.458B (including $563M of severance). Operating margin slipped to 59.1% from 60.7%. If the 'payments hyperscaler' investment cycle persists, margins drift down.
Client incentives paid to banks rose 18% YoY to $4.680B in Q3 FY2026, faster than revenue - evidence that Visa has to pay more to keep issuer relationships, a slow bleed on the take rate.

Regulatory: the Credit Card Competition Act, which would force issuers to enable a non-Visa/non-Mastercard routing option, remains live in Congress; the approved MDL settlement also lets merchants decline premium/commercial cards and surcharge, which could shift mix away from Visa's most profitable products. As of 2026-10-08 the White House was again publicly urging Congress to pass the CCCA (S.3623, still in the Senate Banking Committee) and merchant lobbyists were trying to attach it to other legislation in the lame-duck session; industry sources still call passage unlikely, but the risk is live.

Disruption: account-to-account and real-time rails (FedNow, UPI, Pix), stablecoins and Big Tech wallets could route volume around the card networks over time. Visa is investing to co-opt this, but the outcome is genuinely uncertain.

Cyclicality: consumer spending and especially high-margin cross-border travel volume fall in a recession, and management's Q4 FY2026 guidance already flags tougher FX comparisons, Middle East uncertainty and less FIFA-related revenue.

Reported GAAP earnings are noisy: the nine months to 2026-06-30 included a $1.290B litigation provision and $563M of severance, so the GAAP-vs-non-GAAP gap ($11.76 vs $12.78 TTM) is wide enough to matter to the valuation conclusion.
what_would_break_thesis: GAAP operating margin falls below 55% for two consecutive fiscal quarters (it was 59.1% in Q3 FY2026; this is the erosion-of-pricing-power trigger, tightened from 50% because margin is already drifting).
Net revenue shrinks year-over-year for two consecutive quarters outside a clearly identified macro recession (signals structural volume loss or disruption).
Client incentives grow faster than net revenue for four consecutive quarters (the take rate is being competed away).
Net-debt-to-EBITDA rises above 2.0x (currently ~0.35x) - a sign of balance-sheet deterioration or value-destroying M&A.
Free cash flow turns negative for a full fiscal year, or TTM free cash flow falls more than 25% below the prior year's absent a one-off.

A regulatory ruling, statute (e.g. passage of the Credit Card Competition Act) or settlement that structurally caps network fees or mandates alternative routing in a major market and is expected to cut Visa's net revenue by more than ~15%.

Cross-border volume growth stalls structurally (negative or near-zero constant-dollar growth for four consecutive quarters outside a recession), indicating a permanent loss of the highest-margin business.

Processed transaction growth falls below 3% YoY for two consecutive quarters while global consumer spending is still growing - the clearest early sign of disintermediation by A2A rails or stablecoins.
A serious accounting red flag, restatement, or a material weakness disclosed in internal controls.
catalysts: Q4 and full-year FY2026 earnings on Tuesday 2026-10-27 after the close (webcast 5:00pm ET). This is the single most important date for the thesis: re-run the full refresh the next day with new TTM EPS, FCF, operating margin, client incentives, cross-border volume and the FY2027 outlook. refresh_due is set to 2026-10-28 for this reason.
FY2026 Form 10-K (normally filed in mid-November) - check for litigation-provision updates, material-weakness disclosures and the final MDL settlement accounting.

China domestic clearing: progress through the PBOC/NFRA licence process within the one-year preparation window. Treat as upside optionality only until a licence is issued and revenue appears in filings.
Lame-duck Congress (Nov-Dec 2026): whether the Credit Card Competition Act is attached to must-pass legislation - a direct test of sell trigger #6.

Any market pullback: our buy zone (~$257 at a 12% MoS, ~$239 under the cautious 18% rule) needs a ~37-41% decline on current inputs, so a normal correction will not be enough on its own; fair value has to grow into the price via earnings.
Continued buybacks ($28.4B authorised remaining at 2026-06-30) and growth of value-added services / 'other revenue' (+45% YoY in Q3 FY2026).
